why: D5b ladder E3 parts on olmo-3-7b-instruct (raw)
sample: the map run's cases (cases.jsonl), not resampled
format: suite_v1's: raw text: the user content, a newline and 'Answer:', no template (BJ_FORMAT=raw)

groups.question: the question's tokens after C's changed ones, through the end of the prompt (the instruction, the template's tokens and 'Answer:' included)

read: one forward of the edited prompt, a digit answer's space token appended; role of the top token (b: X's answer, A: the bridge's, other); ld = logit(b) - logit(A); frac = (ld - ld_clean) / (ld_C - ld_clean), ld_clean and ld_C from the unedited clean and C runs
question: At each family's window, which part of the copy carries the bridge: its J-space part or the rest?

parts.full: delta = h_C - h_clean at the question group
parts.lens2: delta's projection on span{v_I, v_X}, the lens's unit vectors of the bridge and X; not_lens2 the rest
parts.jspace: delta's 25-atom signed OMP part over the lens's unit letter-token vectors; not_jspace the rest

controls: each part along a seeded random direction at the same per-position norm (its null); lens2_matched and jspace_matched: per position the part's norm and cosine with delta, the rest a random direction orthogonal to delta (an equal-sized, equally aligned piece of the copy); O's full copy

decision.measures: primary: frac (the logit difference moved, as a fraction of the way to C); secondary: flips (top token X's answer). Per case, each averaged over the window's layers; paired bootstraps over cases
decision.parts: per family and measure: the J-space part's concentration = sum over cases of its effect / sum of (its share of the copy's variance x the full copy's effect), with a case-bootstrap 95% interval (1: it does what its size predicts). Verdict: inside if the lower bound is above 2.0 (it carries at least 2x its share); outside if the upper bound is below 2.0 and not_jspace - jspace is above 0 (paired bootstrap); otherwise inconclusive. The same for lens2 (the bridge's and X's own word vectors). Reported, not decisive: jspace - jspace_matched (an equal-sized, equally aligned piece of the copy) and exp09's rule against the random null (verdict_exp09). Chosen after the smoke runs (8 scenes), before any full run: with the continuous measure, the J-space part beat its random null (2-5 points) and the matched piece (0.3-2 points) in every family while moving the answer about its share of the copy's variance (8-13%), so a significance test alone would call any small piece of the copy 'inside' at n=150
decision.claim_1: variables used by a lookup in the prompt are carried outside the J-space: refuted if BL is inside; supported if BL is outside; the other lookup-used families (RL, BLR, NAMES, CODE) reported the same way; BR, RR and BRL (recall-used) are the comparison
decision.tie_break: BLR and BRL: 'what uses the bridge decides' if BLR is outside and BRL inside; 'where the answer comes from decides' if BLR is inside and BRL outside; otherwise mixed, reported family by family
decision.empty_window: a family with an empty window is not interpreted

calibration.parts: rand_omp: the same 25-atom signed OMP over a random dictionary (as many unit rows as the letter-token dictionary, seeded per layer), the null for the concentration statistic; jspace_wo_own: the J-space part of delta minus its projection on the bridge's and X's lens vectors (control_split's v3)
calibration.why: Zach (2026-10-20) asked for 1.2x as the inside threshold; rand_omp says what concentration the fitting procedure alone gives, so a threshold can be set against it
calibration.decision: fixed before the run: the J-space part is above the fitting null in a family if its concentration's lower bound exceeds rand_omp's upper bound; its effect is the bridge's own words if jspace_wo_own moves the answer less than a quarter as far as jspace
